question: How many identical layers compose the encoder stack in the Transformer model?
expected_answer: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers.

question: What is the output dimension (d_model) produced by all sub-layers and embedding layers in the Transformer?
expected_answer: All sub-layers and embedding layers produce outputs of dimension d_model = 512.

question: What are the three sub-layers in each decoder layer of the Transformer?
expected_answer: Each decoder layer contains a masked multi-head self-attention mechanism, a multi-head attention over the encoder stack output, and a position-wise fully connected feed-forward network.

question: Why is the self-attention sub-layer in the decoder stack masked?
expected_answer: Masking prevents positions from attending to subsequent positions, preserving the auto-regressive property so predictions for position i depend only on known outputs at positions less than i.

question: What is the mathematical formula for Scaled Dot-Product Attention in matrix form?
expected_answer: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q K^T / \sqrt{d_k}) V.

question: Why do the authors scale the dot products by 1 / \sqrt{d_k} in Scaled Dot-Product Attention?
expected_answer: For large values of d_k, dot products grow large in magnitude, pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients; scaling by 1 / \sqrt{d_k} counteracts this effect.

question: In the multi-head attention mechanism with h = 8 parallel heads and d_model = 512, what are the dimensions d_k and d_v?
expected_answer: d_k = d_v = d_model / h = 64.

question: What parameter projection matrix dimensions are used for queries, keys, values, and the multi-head output in Multi-Head Attention?
expected_answer: Projection matrices W_i^Q \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{model} \times d_k}, W_i^K \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{model} \times d_k}, W_i^V \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{model} \times d_v}, and W^O \in \mathbb{R}^{h d_v \times d_{model}}.

question: What are the three distinct ways Multi-Head Attention is applied in the Transformer model?
expected_answer: 1) Encoder-decoder attention where queries come from the previous decoder layer and keys/values come from the encoder output; 2) Encoder self-attention where queries, keys, and values come from the previous encoder layer; 3) Decoder self-attention where positions attend to preceding decoder positions.

question: How is the prevention of leftward information flow implemented inside scaled dot-product attention for decoder self-attention?
expected_answer: By masking out (setting to -\infty) all values in the input of the softmax corresponding to illegal connections.

question: What is the mathematical equation for the position-wise feed-forward network (FFN)?
expected_answer: FFN(x) = max(0, x W_1 + b_1) W_2 + b_2.

question: What are the inner-layer dimensionality (d_ff) and input/output dimensionality (d_model) of the position-wise feed-forward network?
expected_answer: Inner-layer dimensionality d_ff = 2048 and input/output dimensionality d_model = 512.

question: How else can the position-wise feed-forward network be described besides two linear transformations with a ReLU activation?
expected_answer: As two convolutions with kernel size 1.

question: What multiplication factor is applied to the weights in the embedding layers of the Transformer?
expected_answer: In the embedding layers, the shared weights are multiplied by \sqrt{d_{model}}.

question: What are the trigonometric formulas used for calculating Positional Encodings at even (2i) and odd (2i+1) dimensions?
expected_answer: PE_{(pos, 2i)} = \sin(pos / 10000^{2i / d_{model}}) and PE_{(pos, 2i+1)} = \cos(pos / 10000^{2i / d_{model}}).

question: Why did the authors choose sinusoidal positional encodings over learned positional embeddings?
expected_answer: Because sinusoidal encodings may allow the model to extrapolate to sequence lengths longer than the ones encountered during training.

question: What is the per-layer computational complexity for a Self-Attention layer compared to a Recurrent layer?
expected_answer: Self-Attention complexity per layer is O(n^2 \cdot d), whereas Recurrent layer complexity is O(n \cdot d^2).

question: What is the minimum number of sequential operations required for Self-Attention layers versus Recurrent layers?
expected_answer: Self-Attention requires O(1) sequential operations, whereas Recurrent layers require O(n) sequential operations.

question: What is the maximum path length between any two input and output positions in a Self-Attention layer versus a dilated Convolutional layer?
expected_answer: Maximum path length is O(1) for Self-Attention and O(\log_k(n)) for dilated Convolutional layers.

question: Under what condition are self-attention layers faster in computational complexity than recurrent layers?
expected_answer: Self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d.

question: How can self-attention be restricted to handle very long sequences, and what is the resulting maximum path length?
expected_answer: By restricting self-attention to considering only a neighborhood of size r in the input sequence centered around the output position, which increases the maximum path length to O(n/r).

question: What BLEU scores did the Transformer achieve on the WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks?
expected_answer: 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French.

question: How does the number of operations required to relate signals from two arbitrary positions grow in ConvS2S and ByteNet relative to position distance?
expected_answer: The number of operations grows linearly for ConvS2S and logarithmically for ByteNet.

question: What hardware setup and training steps were used for the base Transformer model versus the big Transformer model?
expected_answer: The base model was trained on 8 NVIDIA P100 GPUs for 100,000 steps (12 hours), while the big model was trained for 300,000 steps (3.5 days).

question: What hyperparameter settings were configured for the Adam optimizer during model training?
expected_answer: \beta_1 = 0.9, \beta_2 = 0.98, and \epsilon = 10^{-9}.

question: What equation defines the learning rate schedule over training steps?
expected_answer: lrate = d_{model}^{-0.5} \cdot \min(step\_num^{-0.5}, step\_num \cdot warmup\steps^{-1.5}) with warmup\steps = 4000.

question: What residual dropout rate and label smoothing value were applied during training?
expected_answer: A residual dropout rate P{drop} = 0.1 for the base model and a label smoothing value \epsilon{ls} = 0.1.

question: What beam search configuration (beam size and length penalty \alpha) was used during inference for translation?
expected_answer: A beam size of 4 and length penalty \alpha = 0.6.

question: What F1 score did the 4-layer Transformer achieve on Section 23 of the WSJ constituency parsing task in the semi-supervised setting?
expected_answer: An F1 score of 92.7.

question: Where is the official codebase repository for training and evaluating the Transformer models available?
expected_answer: [https://github.com/tensorflow/tensor2tensor](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensor2tensor).
